notes: 146 studies on writing about hard things. The honest result: it helps, on average, a little. That's not a reason to stop journaling. It's a reason to care about how you do it. This week's essay is about the how.

Marcus Aurelius rarely wrote "I" in his notebook. He wrote "thou", like a teacher talking to a student who keeps making the same mistake. Modern research on self-distancing suggests that's where some of the benefit lives.
If you've written about the same thing three times this month, you're not reflecting any more. You're rehearsing. Write the next page in the second person and see what changes.
